questions.question: Which description fits the **EnrollmentResponse** resource?
options: This resource provides enrollment and plan details from the processing of an EnrollmentRequest resource.
Financial instrument which may be used to reimburse or pay for health care products and services.

This resource provides patient and insurance coverage information to an insurer for them to respond, in the form of an CoverageEligibilityResponse, with information regarding whether the stated coverage is…
This resource provides the insurance enrollment details to the insurer regarding a specified coverage.
questions.explanation: **EnrollmentResponse**: This resource provides enrollment and plan details from the processing of an EnrollmentRequest resource. The other descriptions belong to **Coverage**, **CoverageEligibilityRequest**, **EnrollmentRequest**.

questions.question: Which resource matches this definition from the specification? “This resource provides enrollment and plan details from the processing of an EnrollmentRequest resource.”
questions.explanation: This is the definition of **EnrollmentResponse** (Financial › Support).

questions.question: Where does **EnrollmentResponse** sit in the FHIR R4 resource list?
questions.explanation: **EnrollmentResponse** is in **Financial › Support**: Insurance cover and enrolment: who pays for the patient’s care (Coverage), and checking eligibility before care is given.

questions.question: Which statement about required elements in **EnrollmentResponse** is true?
options: No top-level element is required: every element has a minimum cardinality of 0
questions.explanation: Every top-level element of EnrollmentResponse is optional (`0..1` or `0..*`) in the base resource. Profiles can make elements required for a particular use.

questions.question: Which element of **EnrollmentResponse** is a **modifier** (?!), so receiving systems must not ignore it?
questions.explanation: Modifier elements of EnrollmentResponse: `status`. `status`: active | cancelled | draft | entered-in-error. A modifier can change the meaning of the whole resource: for example, a status of `entered-in-error` means the data must not be used.
